issue: Under First Step Act § 404(b), may or must a district court apply a judicial decision issued after the defendant's original sentencing when ruling on a motion to reduce a crack cocaine sentence?
provision: First Step Act of 2018, Pub. L. No. 115-391, § 404(b)

sides.position: Section 404(b) authorizes but does not require a district court to apply intervening judicial decisions when ruling on a First Step Act motion.
cases: United States v. Kelley, 962 F.3d 470 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Fowowe, 1 F.4th 522 (7th Cir. 2021)

sides.position: A district court ruling on a First Step Act motion is not free to reduce a covered offense sentence based on changes in law beyond those mandated by §§ 2 and 3 of the Fair Sentencing Act.
cases: United States v. Denson, 963 F.3d 1080 (11th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Taylor, 982 F.3d 1296 (11th Cir. 2020)

this_court: Authorizes but does not require application of intervening judicial decisions, joining the Sixth Circuit and rejecting the Eleventh Circuit's narrower reading.
quote: This question is one narrow issue within a broader, emerging circuit split on the parameters of district court § 404(b) motion evaluation.
cite: United States v. Olaitan Fowowe, 1 F.4th 522 (7th Cir. 2021)
